plain.en: Explain it simply, in about 30 seconds.
plain.tip: 先講結論，再給一兩個理由。用短句。

patient.en: Explain it to a patient or a family member. Use an everyday comparison.
patient.tip: 不用縮寫、不講數字，找一個生活上的比喻。

nurse.en: Explain it to a ward nurse. What does it mean for daily care?
nurse.tip: 講「你會看到什麼、要做什麼」。

engineer.en: Explain it to an engineer. Focus on how it works.
engineer.tip: 講訊號、機制、因果，可以用技術名詞。

clinician.en: Explain it to another doctor. Lead with the data.
clinician.tip: 第一句就給數字，再講意義和界線。

skeptic.en: Someone in the audience challenges you. Answer the question.
skeptic.tip: 先肯定問題，再直接回答，最後給一個證據。

story.zh: 從一個故事或經驗講起
story.en: Start with a story or an experience, then make the point.
story.tip: 「我們一開始…後來…所以…」的順序。

honest.zh: 不知道答案時誠實回答
honest.en: You don't have the exact answer. Answer honestly and helpfully.
honest.tip: 承認、給你知道的部分、提議會後再談。

oneliner.tip: 一句、大約 15–20 個字，只留最核心的意思。

concepts.title_en: Why sleep testing is so hard
concepts.title_zh: 為什麼睡眠檢查這麼難
concepts.essence: 傳統睡眠檢查又慢、又麻煩、又不自然：要等 1–2 個月、貼感測器常超過 40 分鐘、要接 20 多條線，還要在陌生的環境睡覺。

ideas.zh: 病人要等很久（1–2 個月）
ideas.en: Patients wait one or two months for a sleep test.

ideas.zh: 貼感測器很久（超過 40 分鐘）、很多線
ideas.en: Putting on the sensors often takes more than 40 minutes, with many wires.

ideas.zh: 在不自然的環境睡、讓人焦慮
ideas.en: Patients have to sleep in a very unnatural setting, and it makes them anxious.
But we need objective data to confirm sleep-disordered breathing.

terms.note: 重音在 -NAH-：pah-lee-sahm-NAH-gruh-fee；口語直接說 P-S-G 也可以
disordered 重音在 -SOR-；breathing 的 th 要濁音 /ð/
HAS-sul；「很麻煩」說 a real hassle，不要說 very trouble

connectors: Let me start with a simple question.
That's why we need something simpler.

mistakes.why: 數量大於一要用複數 months。
trouble 是名詞，不能用 very 修飾；口語常說 a real hassle。

mistakes.good: Patients need to wait. / The patient needs to wait.
mistakes.why: 第三人稱單數動詞要加 -s，或主詞改複數。

models.plain: Sleep testing is hard for three reasons. First, patients wait one or two months for a sleep study. Second, putting on all the sensors often takes more than 40 minutes, and that makes people anxious. And third, they have to sleep in a lab, which is nothing like their own bed.
models.patient: Imagine trying to fall asleep with more than twenty wires on your head and body, in a strange room. That's what a standard sleep test feels like. And you may wait a month or two just to get a bed.
models.clinician: We need objective data to confirm sleep-disordered breathing, but PSG is a bottleneck. It needs 20 or more wires, the setup often takes more than 40 minutes, and patients wait one to two months.
models.skeptic: PSG is still the gold standard, and we still need it. The problem is access. Patients wait one or two months, the setup takes more than 40 minutes, and they have to sleep in a very unnatural setting.
models.oneliner: Sleep tests are slow to get, take a long time to set up, and make people sleep in a very unnatural setting.

concepts.challenge: PSG is the gold standard. Why not just use it?
connSay: Let me start with a simple question.
That's why we need something simpler.

concepts.essence: 雷達從 Tx 發出訊號、在 Rx 收到反射；胸部一點點的起伏會改變反射訊號的飛行時間（ToF）和相位，我們從這些變化重建呼吸波形，完全不用接線。

ideas.zh: 雷達發出訊號、收到反射
ideas.en: The radar sends a signal and picks up the reflection.

ideas.zh: 胸部動一點點，訊號就改變
ideas.en: When the chest moves a little, the received signal changes.

ideas.zh: 改變的是飛行時間和相位
ideas.en: It changes the time of flight and the phase of the signal.
From those changes, we rebuild the breathing signal.
There are no wires, and nothing touches the patient.

terms.note: of 弱讀成 /əv/，三個字連在一起唸
結尾是 /z/，和 face /feɪs/ 不同
GHz 唸 gigahertz（GIG-uh-herts），不要逐字母唸 G-H-Z

mistakes.why: 主詞是單數 the radar，動詞加 -s。

mistakes.good: the signal bounces back / is reflected
mistakes.why: reflect 已經有「反射回來」的意思，口語常用 bounces back。
breath 是「一口氣」，當形容詞修飾 signal 時用 breathing。

models.plain: Here's how it works. The radar sends out a signal, and it bounces back from the body. Every time the chest moves, even a little, the returning signal changes. From those changes, we rebuild the breathing wave, with no wires at all.
models.patient: It's a bit like a bat using echoes. The device sends out a signal and listens for the echo. When your chest goes up and down, the echo changes slightly, and that tells us how you're breathing. Nothing touches you.
models.engineer: It's a 24-GHz continuous-wave radar. We transmit from Tx and receive the reflection at Rx. Chest movement changes the time of flight and the phase of the received signal, and from those changes we reconstruct the breathing waveform.
models.skeptic: Because the radar doesn't need a big movement. Even a tiny shift of the chest changes the phase of the reflected signal. We track those small changes, breath by breath, and turn them into a breathing wave.
models.oneliner: The radar reads tiny chest movements from its reflected signal and turns them into a breathing wave, with no wires.

concepts.challenge: How can a radar see something as small as breathing?

concepts.title_en: Setting it up at the bedside
concepts.essence: 雷達可以裝在床頭上方的牆上、支架或落地架：醫院固定床用壁掛支架（Option A），居家用好移動的落地架（Option B）；距離 75–90 公分，完全不碰病人。

ideas.zh: 裝在牆上、支架或落地架
ideas.en: It goes on the wall above the bed, on an arm, or on a floor stand.

ideas.zh: 醫院用壁掛、居家用落地架
ideas.en: Wall bracket for fixed hospital beds; floor stand for homes.
The radar is set at 75 to 90 centimeters.
Nothing touches the patient.

terms.note: 「裝在牆上」說 mount it on the wall，不說 stick
兩個字都要清楚，stand 的 /æ/ 張大嘴

mistakes.bad: stick the radar on the wall
mistakes.good: mount the radar on the wall
mistakes.why: stick 是「黏」；裝設備用 mount。
mistakes.say: mount the radar on the wall

mistakes.why: 單位要用複數。

mistakes.good: It's best for homes. / It works well at home.
mistakes.why: suitable for home 文法偏書面又少冠詞；口語說 best for homes 或 at home。
「在家」固定說 at home。

models.plain: Setting it up is simple. In the hospital, we mount the radar on the wall above the bed. At home, we use a floor stand that's easy to move. Either way, the radar sits about 75 to 90 centimeters away, and nothing touches the patient.
models.nurse: For you on the ward, there's nothing to attach. No wires, no patches. The radar is on a wall bracket above the bed, at about 75 to 90 centimeters. You don't have to fix sensors in the middle of the night.
models.patient: You just sleep as usual. There's a small device on a stand next to your bed, or on the wall. It doesn't touch you, and you don't need to wear anything.
models.skeptic: It does matter. We set the radar at 75 to 90 centimeters. For fixed hospital beds, the wall bracket keeps it in place. At home, the floor stand is easy to move, so we just place it within that range.
models.oneliner: Put it on the wall or on a stand, 75 to 90 centimeters away, and the patient wears nothing.

concepts.challenge: Does the position of the radar have to be exact?

concepts.title_en: Airflow vs. chest motion: the blind spot
concepts.title_zh: 氣流 vs. 胸部動作：最大的盲點
concepts.essence: 標準睡眠檢查看的是「氣流」，雷達看的是「胸部動作」，兩種訊號不一樣；每個人體型、睡姿不同；阻塞時呼吸道塞住、沒有氣流，但身體用力呼吸、胸部又動起來——所以用胸部動作大小判斷呼吸中止誤差很大。

ideas.zh: 睡眠檢查看氣流，雷達看胸部
ideas.en: Sleep tests watch airflow, while radar watches the chest.
Every patient is different: body size and sleep position.

ideas.zh: 阻塞時沒氣流，但胸部還在用力動
ideas.en: During obstruction there is no airflow, but the chest keeps moving as the body struggles.

ideas.zh: 所以用動作大小判斷會錯很多
ideas.en: So judging apnea by the size of chest motion has a big error.

terms.note: 美式 AP-nee-uh，重音在第一音節

mistakes.why: 單數主詞，動詞加 -s。
「盲點」英文固定說 blind spot。

mistakes.bad: Because the airway is blocked, so the airflow stops.
mistakes.good: Because the airway is blocked, the airflow stops.
mistakes.why: 中文「因為…所以…」英文只能用一個：because 或 so。
mistakes.say: Because the airway is blocked, the airflow stops.

models.plain: Here's the catch. Sleep tests watch airflow, but radar watches the chest. During an obstructive event, the airway is blocked, so airflow stops. But the body keeps trying to breathe, so the chest still moves. If we judge apnea by how big the chest motion is, we get it wrong.
models.engineer: The scoring rules are defined on airflow: apnea is airflow stopping, hypopnea is airflow getting shallow. Our signal is chest motion, and its size depends on body size and sleep position. And during obstruction, the effort to breathe can increase. So size-based rules don't transfer. That was our biggest blind spot.
models.patient: Think of a blocked straw. You suck harder and harder, your cheeks move a lot, but no air comes through. The chest does the same thing when the airway closes. So the radar can see a lot of movement even when there's no air.
models.skeptic: Not always. In an obstructive event, the airway is blocked, so no air gets in. But the body struggles to breathe, so the chest moves again. A standard test sees no airflow, while the radar sees motion. That's exactly why chest motion alone can fool you.
models.oneliner: Sleep tests watch airflow, the radar watches the chest, and during an obstruction the chest can move with no air.

concepts.challenge: If the chest is moving, isn't the patient breathing?

concepts.title_zh: 事件結尾的「恢復大呼吸」
concepts.essence: 解法不是看動作大小，而是找「典型的胸部動作變化模式」；這個模式的結尾是 recovery surge：事件結束、呼吸道打開，人會吸一口很大的氣。我們和工程團隊的第一年試了很多方法都失敗，幾乎放棄。

ideas.zh: 找典型的變化模式（不是看大小）
ideas.en: The radar has to spot a typical pattern of chest-motion changes.
The pattern ends with the recovery surge.

ideas.zh: 呼吸道打開、吸一口大氣
ideas.en: When an event ends, the airway opens, and the person takes one big breath.

ideas.zh: 第一年試很多方法、差點放棄
ideas.en: In our first year, nothing worked and we almost gave up.

terms.note: take a big breath（名詞，清音 θ）；breathe normally（動詞，濁音 ð）

mistakes.why: 講過去的經驗要用過去式。
breath 是名詞，breathe 是動詞。
單數主詞動詞加 -s；「事件結束」常用 ends。

models.plain: Instead of measuring how big the chest motion is, we look for a typical pattern. The chest motion drops, the body struggles, and then the event ends with a recovery surge: the airway opens, and the person takes one big breath. That pattern is what the radar picks up.
models.story: In our first year with the engineering team, we tried many methods, and nothing worked. We almost gave up. Then we changed the question. We stopped asking how big each breath is, and started looking for the pattern that ends with one big recovery breath.
models.patient: After the airway has been blocked for a while, your body suddenly opens it and takes a huge breath, almost like a gasp. That big breath is like a signature. The radar learns to spot it, night after night.
models.skeptic: We don't rely on one big breath alone. We look at the whole pattern: the chest motion drops, the effort builds, and then it ends with a recovery surge. It's the sequence that matters, not a single breath.
models.oneliner: We spot each event by its pattern, and the pattern ends with one big recovery breath.

concepts.challenge: How do you know a big breath means an apnea, and not just a deep sigh?

concepts.essence: 研究一（2024 年發表）在控制良好的睡眠實驗室，讓 196 位病人同時做 PSG 和雷達，相關係數 r = 0.91；中重度 OSA 準確率 90.3%、重度 OSA 92.4%、多分類平均 83.7%。

ideas.zh: 在醫院和 PSG 同時比較
ideas.en: We compared the radar side by side with PSG in the hospital.
We tested 196 patients.
The correlation was strong: r = 0.91.

ideas.zh: 嚴重度準確率（中重度 90.3%、重度 92.4%）
ideas.en: Accuracy was 90.3% for moderate-to-severe OSA and 92.4% for severe OSA.

terms.note: cor-uh-LAY-shun；「強相關」說 a strong correlation
唸 “r equals zero point nine one” 或 “an r of point nine one”，不要唸 ninety-one
moderate 的 -ate 弱讀 /ət/；severe 重音在後 se-VERE
三個字連著唸，重音在最後的 side

mistakes.why: 數字後面的名詞要複數。
high 不算錯，但口語和論文更常說 strong correlation。
up to 是「最高可達」，會讓聽眾以為是挑最好的數字；研究結果用過去式直接講。

models.clinician: In Study 1, we ran the radar side by side with full PSG in 196 patients in the sleep lab. The correlation was strong, r = 0.91. For moderate-to-severe OSA, the accuracy was 90.3%, and for severe OSA, it was 92.4%.
models.plain: First, we tested it in the hospital, where everything is controlled. 196 patients slept with full PSG and the radar at the same time. The two results lined up very well, with a correlation of 0.91.
models.patient: We asked almost two hundred patients to do the standard hospital sleep test and the radar at the same time, on the same night. The radar's results matched the standard test very closely.
models.skeptic: That's a fair point. Correlation isn't everything, so we also looked at accuracy for severity. For moderate-to-severe OSA it was 90.3%, and for severe OSA 92.4%. And that's why we use it as a screen, not as a replacement for PSG.
models.oneliner: Side by side with PSG in 196 patients, the radar correlated at r = 0.91.

concepts.challenge: A correlation of 0.91 can still hide big errors. Is that enough?

concepts.essence: 研究二把雷達帶回家：居家什麼都無法控制（睡姿、厚被子、噪音、沒有技術人員）。80 位病人、147 晚、沒有人員在場，與居家睡眠檢查（HSAT）比較，Spearman ρ = 0.87；平均大約低 5 events/h；重度 OSA 準確率約 93%。

ideas.en: At home, nothing is controlled: positions, blankets, noise.
There is no technician and no staff on site.
80 patients, 147 nights.
Compared with HSAT, the Spearman correlation was rho = 0.87.
On average, it was about 5 events per hour lower.

terms.note: 和 row 同音；“rho equals zero point eight seven”

terms.zh: 居家睡眠呼吸中止檢查
terms.note: 可以說 home sleep apnea testing，第一次出現時講全名

mistakes.why: 數字後面的名詞要複數。

mistakes.good: with no one supervising / nobody supervises
mistakes.why: nobody 是單數，或改成分詞片語。
中文「沒有人」在這裡指沒有工作人員，英文說 no staff / no technician。

models.plain: Then we took it home. Real homes are messy: different sleep positions, thick blankets, noise, and no technician. We tested 80 patients over 147 nights, with no staff on site. Compared with home sleep apnea testing, the correlation was still strong, rho = 0.87.
models.clinician: Study 2 was 80 patients and 147 nights, unsupervised, compared with HSAT. Spearman's rho was 0.87, with p < 0.01. On average, the radar read about 5 events per hour lower. For severe OSA, the accuracy was about 93%.
models.patient: You don't have to come to the hospital. We bring the device to your home, you sleep in your own bed, and nobody needs to be there. In our study, the results at home were still close to the standard home sleep test.
models.skeptic: That was exactly our worry. At home we have blankets, different positions, noise, and nobody watching. So we needed robust signal processing. Even so, the correlation with HSAT was rho = 0.87, and on average it was only about 5 events per hour lower.
models.oneliner: At home, with no staff on site, it still tracked HSAT closely, with rho = 0.87.

concepts.challenge: Homes are noisy and messy. How can it still work there?

concepts.essence: 裝置已通過 TFDA：bRDI ≥ 30 只用來「篩檢可疑重度 OSA」，在 30 這個切點，敏感度和特異度都是 90.5%；它不能單獨診斷 OSA。

ideas.en: The device is TFDA cleared.

ideas.zh: 用來篩檢可疑重度 OSA
ideas.en: It is used only as a screen for suspected severe OSA.
The cut-off is a bRDI of 30 or more.
At that cut-off, sensitivity and specificity are both 90.5%.
It does not diagnose OSA on its own.

terms.note: CLEAR-ence；「通過 TFDA」說 It is TFDA cleared
當動詞：it screens for suspected severe OSA

mistakes.bad: TFDA approved, so it can diagnose OSA.
mistakes.good: It's TFDA cleared as a screen for suspected severe OSA.
mistakes.why: 核可範圍是「篩檢」，不能說成診斷。
mistakes.say: It's TFDA cleared as a screen for suspected severe OSA.

mistakes.why: cut-off 本身就是名詞「切點」，不用再加 point。
兩個主詞用 are；加 both 更清楚。

models.plain: The device is TFDA cleared, but only as a screen. If the bRDI is 30 or more, we flag the patient as suspected severe OSA. At that cut-off, sensitivity and specificity are both 90.5%. It does not diagnose OSA on its own.
models.patient: Think of it like a smoke alarm. It tells us when something might be wrong, so we know who needs a full sleep test first. But it doesn't give you the final diagnosis. Your doctor still confirms it with a standard test.
models.nurse: If the morning report shows a bRDI of 30 or more, that's a flag for suspected severe OSA. It's a screen, not a diagnosis, so the next step is to tell the doctor, and the doctor decides on a full sleep test.
models.skeptic: No. TFDA cleared it as a screen for suspected severe OSA, not as a diagnostic test. It helps us find who needs further testing, with 90.5% sensitivity and specificity at a cut-off of 30. The diagnosis still needs a standard sleep test.
models.oneliner: It's a TFDA-cleared screen for suspected severe OSA, not a diagnosis.

concepts.challenge: So can I use this instead of PSG to diagnose OSA?

concepts.title_en: Around the clock: dashboard and alerts
concepts.title_zh: 全天候平台與 LINE 警示
concepts.essence: 裝好之後 24 小時運作：資料經 Wi-Fi 不斷傳送；臨床儀表板一次看到每位病人的狀態、動作和異常生命徵象；異常數值或離床會自動發 LINE 通知；每天早上產生前一晚的報告（bRDI、睡眠時間、PB% 等）。

ideas.zh: 資料不斷經 Wi-Fi 傳送
ideas.en: The radar sends data nonstop over Wi-Fi.

ideas.zh: 儀表板一次看所有病人
ideas.en: The dashboard shows each patient in one place.

ideas.zh: 異常或離床自動 LINE 通知
ideas.en: Staff get an automatic LINE alert for abnormal values or bed exits.

ideas.zh: 每天早上有前一晚報告
ideas.en: Every morning, the radar makes a report from the night before.

terms.note: a patient gets out of bed = a bed exit

mistakes.why: staff 是集合名詞，不加 -s。

mistakes.bad: when the patient leave the bed
mistakes.good: when a patient gets out of bed
mistakes.why: 單數主詞動詞加 -s；「離床」口語是 gets out of bed。
mistakes.say: when a patient gets out of bed

mistakes.good: the nurses get a LINE alert
mistakes.why: notify 是動詞，用「誰收到 alert」的說法比較自然。
mistakes.say: the nurses get a LINE alert

models.nurse: Once it's installed, it runs around the clock. You'll see every patient on one dashboard: status, movement, and any abnormal vital signs. If a value is abnormal or a patient gets out of bed, you get a LINE alert right away.
models.plain: The radar sends data nonstop over Wi-Fi. A dashboard shows all the patients in one place, and the system sends automatic LINE alerts for abnormal values or bed exits. Every morning, it also makes a report from the night before.
models.clinician: In practice, the radar streams data over Wi-Fi around the clock. The dashboard shows each bed's status, and staff get LINE alerts for abnormal values or bed exits. Every morning, the team also gets a report for each bed: bRDI, sleep time, PB percentage, and the average PB cycle length.
models.patient: While you sleep, nobody needs to come in and check wires. The device quietly watches your breathing, and if something looks wrong, the nurses get a message on their phones right away.
models.skeptic: The alerts are only for abnormal values or bed exits, not for every breath. And instead of walking from bed to bed, the staff can see everyone on one dashboard. So the idea is to focus their attention, not to add more work.
models.oneliner: It runs around the clock, shows everyone on one dashboard, and sends LINE alerts when something is wrong.

concepts.challenge: Won't all these alerts just add to the nurses' workload?

concepts.essence: 週期性呼吸（PB，也叫 Cheyne–Stokes）是呼吸「漸強又漸弱」：一段大呼吸、接著呼吸中止，一再重複；一段大呼吸加一次中止是一個循環，它的時間叫 PB cycle length。常見於心衰竭；雷達可以每晚自動量測。

ideas.en: In periodic breathing, the breathing grows and fades.

ideas.zh: 大呼吸後接呼吸中止，一再重複
ideas.en: A phase of heavy breathing, then an apnea, again and again.
The time one cycle takes is the PB cycle length.
Periodic breathing is often seen in heart failure.
From the radar signal, we can measure the cycle length automatically, night after night.

terms.note: length 結尾 /ŋθ/，舌尖輕碰牙齒
FAIL-yer；說 patients with heart failure 比 heart failure patients 更溫和

mistakes.bad: the breathing become bigger and smaller
mistakes.why: 單數主詞要 becomes；grows and fades 是更道地的說法。
「一個週期的時間」英文是 cycle length。
Cheyne 唸起來跟 chain 一樣。

models.plain: Periodic breathing means the breathing grows and fades. There's a phase of heavy breathing, then an apnea, again and again. One heavy phase plus one apnea is one cycle, and the time it takes is the cycle length. It's often seen in heart failure.
models.patient: Imagine waves on a beach: a big wave, then calm, then another big wave. Some people breathe like that in their sleep, strong breaths, then a pause, over and over. We often see this in people with heart problems.
models.engineer: On the raw radar signal, you can see the breathing grow and fade, over and over. Our algorithm detects each cycle, so the cycle length is measured automatically, night after night, from a continuous signal. And periodic breathing is often seen in heart failure.
models.skeptic: There's some overlap, because each cycle includes an apnea. But the pattern is different: the breathing grows and fades in a smooth cycle. That pattern, also called Cheyne-Stokes breathing, is often seen in heart failure, so it may tell us something about the heart.
models.oneliner: Periodic breathing grows and fades in cycles, and the cycle length may tell us something about the heart.

concepts.challenge: Isn't periodic breathing just another kind of sleep apnea?

concepts.title_en: Why breathing swings: high loop gain
concepts.title_zh: 為什麼呼吸會擺盪：high loop gain
concepts.essence: 呼吸由一個回饋迴路控制（大腦發訊號→肺改變 CO₂→血液把變化帶回感受器）。High loop gain 就是這個迴路「反應過度」。兩個主因：呼吸道阻力（OSA）和心衰竭（血流慢、訊號晚到，大腦總是慢一步：太多、又太少）。雷達不量 CO₂ 或血氧，只看呼吸模式。

ideas.en: Our breathing is run by a feedback loop.
High loop gain means the loop overreacts.
First reason: airway resistance, like in OSA.

ideas.zh: 原因二：心衰竭→訊號晚到、慢一步
ideas.en: Second: in heart failure, blood moves slowly, so signals arrive late.
Our radar does not measure CO2 or oxygen; it only sees the breathing pattern.

mistakes.bad: The brain always late one step.
mistakes.good: The brain is always one step behind.
mistakes.why: 中文「慢一步」英文是 one step behind，而且需要 be 動詞。
mistakes.say: The brain is always one step behind.

mistakes.why: less 是比較級；和 too 連用要說 too little。

mistakes.good: blood moves more slowly / blood flow is slow
mistakes.why: 缺動詞；slow 是形容詞。

models.plain: Our breathing is run by a feedback loop, and high loop gain means the loop overreacts. There are two main reasons. In OSA, the airway keeps closing and opening. In heart failure, blood moves slowly, so the signals arrive late, and the brain is always one step behind: too much, then too little.
models.patient: It's like a shower where the water takes a long time to change temperature. You turn it hot, nothing happens, so you turn it more. Then it's way too hot, so you turn it cold. When the heart is weak, the brain controls breathing the same way: always a little late, too much, then too little.
models.engineer: Think of a control system with a long delay. When the heart is weak, circulation is slow, so the sensors that control breathing get the CO2 signal late. The controller overcorrects, and the system swings. That swing is what we see as periodic breathing.
models.skeptic: No. Just to be clear, our radar does not measure CO2 or oxygen. It only sees the breathing pattern. The loop-gain idea explains that pattern: when the heart is weak, the signals arrive late, so the breathing loop overreacts. The radar measures the cycle length of those swings.
models.oneliner: When the heart is weak, the breathing control loop reacts too late and too much, so breathing swings.

concepts.challenge: Does the radar measure CO2 to show this?

concepts.title_zh: 研究三：呼吸與心臟的關聯
concepts.essence: 研究三（72 位病人，2025 年 IEEE JTEHM）：雷達抓到異常呼吸、特別是週期性呼吸時，和較低的 LVEF 有關；PB 週期每長 1 秒，NT-proBNP 高 158.49 pg/mL。這些都只是「臨床關聯」，還沒有驗證可以用來診斷或預測。

ideas.en: Study 3 had 72 patients.

ideas.zh: 週期性呼吸和較低 LVEF 有關
ideas.en: Periodic breathing was linked to a lower LVEF.
These are associations only.

ideas.zh: 尚未驗證能診斷或預測
ideas.en: It isn't validated yet for diagnosis or prediction.

ideas.zh: PB 週期長 1 秒 → NT-proBNP 高 158.49
ideas.en: If the PB cycle is one second longer, NT-proBNP goes up 158.49 pg/mL.

terms.note: uh-so-see-AY-shun；說 associated with，不說 associated to
逐字母唸；全名 left ventricular ejection fraction

connectors: Now let's turn to the heart.
That's a big change, for just one second.
It's an association, not a diagnosis.

mistakes.good: is associated with a lower LVEF
mistakes.why: related 搭 to；正式一點用 associated with。
mistakes.say: is associated with a lower LVEF

mistakes.bad: The radar can predict heart failure.
mistakes.good: It's linked to lower LVEF, but it isn't validated for prediction.
mistakes.why: 目前只是關聯，不能說可以預測。
mistakes.say: It's linked to lower LVEF, but it isn't validated for prediction.

mistakes.why: 英文量詞放在形容詞前面：one second longer。

models.plain: In Study 3, with 72 patients, we asked whether breathing can tell us about the heart. When the radar picked up periodic breathing, it was linked to a lower LVEF. Just to be clear, it's an association. It isn't validated yet for diagnosis or prediction.
models.clinician: In our 2025 paper, a PB cycle one second longer was associated with NT-proBNP 158.49 picograms per milliliter higher, and LVEF 0.21% lower. These are clinical associations only, not a validated predictor.
models.story: We put the radar in the cardiology ward, and we really saw a lot of Cheyne-Stokes breathing. So we asked: can the breathing pattern tell us how well the heart pumps? We found that periodic breathing was associated with a lower LVEF. It's an early-warning idea, not a diagnosis.
models.patient: Your breathing at night may give us clues about your heart. In our study, people whose breathing went up and down in cycles tended to have weaker heart pumping. But for now it's only a clue, not a test for heart failure.
models.skeptic: No, not yet. What we found are associations: periodic breathing was linked to a lower LVEF and a higher NT-proBNP. That makes it an interesting early-warning idea, but it isn't validated for diagnosis or prediction.
models.oneliner: Periodic breathing on the radar is linked to weaker heart function, but it's an association, not a diagnosis.

concepts.challenge: Are you saying the radar can predict heart failure?
connSay: Now let's turn to the heart.
That's a big change, for just one second.
It's an association, not a diagnosis.

concepts.title_zh: 結論：帶回家的四個重點
concepts.essence: 四個重點：一、無接觸，24 GHz 雷達可以每晚監測、什麼都不用戴；二、和標準檢查一致（醫院 r = 0.91、居家 ρ = 0.87）；三、TFDA 核可的可疑重度 OSA 篩檢（敏感度 90.5%）；四、週期性呼吸和心臟功能受損有關聯，也許能幫我們看心臟。

ideas.en: It's contactless and can monitor breathing night after night.
It's consistent with standard tests: r = 0.91 in the hospital and rho = 0.87 at home.

ideas.zh: TFDA 核可的重度 OSA 篩檢
ideas.en: It's a TFDA-cleared screen for suspected severe OSA.

ideas.zh: 週期性呼吸和心臟有關聯
ideas.en: Periodic breathing is associated with cardiac impairment.

terms.note: 口語：What should you take home?

connectors: I'm happy to take your questions.

mistakes.good: Thank you for listening. / Thank you very much.
mistakes.why: listening 前面不加 your。
不算錯，但口頭演講用 To wrap up 比較自然。

mistakes.good: It may help us watch the heart, too.
mistakes.why: 心臟發現只是關聯，結論也要守住界線。
mistakes.say: It may help us watch the heart, too.

models.plain: To wrap up, four points. It's contactless, so we can monitor breathing night after night. It agrees with standard tests: r = 0.91 in the hospital and rho = 0.87 at home. It's a TFDA-cleared screen for suspected severe OSA. And periodic breathing is linked to the heart.
models.patient: In short: a small device can watch your breathing every night without touching you. It matches the standard tests well, it can tell us who may have severe sleep apnea, and it may even give us clues about the heart.
models.clinician: Three numbers to remember: r = 0.91 against PSG, rho = 0.87 against HSAT at home, and 90.5% sensitivity as a TFDA-cleared screen for suspected severe OSA. Plus an association between periodic breathing and cardiac impairment.
models.skeptic: It's contactless, so patients wear nothing, and we can monitor every night instead of one night in a lab. It's consistent with PSG and home testing, and it's a TFDA-cleared screen for suspected severe OSA. And it may even help us watch the heart.
models.oneliner: Nothing to wear, consistent with standard tests, a TFDA-cleared screen for severe OSA, and a possible window on the heart.

concepts.challenge: If you had 30 seconds to convince a hospital director, what would you say?
connSay: I'm happy to take your questions.

concepts.essence: 誠實講限制：它是篩檢不是診斷；雷達不量血氧或 CO₂，只看呼吸模式；居家平均約低 5 events/h；心臟的發現只是關聯。篩檢陽性時仍要做標準睡眠檢查。

ideas.en: It's a screen, not a diagnosis.
It doesn't measure oxygen or CO2.
At home it read about 5 events per hour lower on average.
The heart findings are associations only.
When the screen is positive, we still do a standard sleep test.

mistakes.why: 泛指氧氣不加 the；口語常用 doesn’t。
說 one limit is that… 比較自然、也不會聽起來只有一個限制。
界線：它是篩檢，不取代 PSG。

models.skeptic: Good question. There are a few. First, it's a screen, not a diagnosis. Second, the radar doesn't measure oxygen or CO2. It only sees the breathing pattern. Third, at home it read about 5 events per hour lower on average. And the heart findings are associations only.
models.plain: To be honest, it doesn't do everything. It doesn't measure oxygen, and it doesn't diagnose OSA on its own. Its job is to screen for suspected severe OSA and to watch breathing night after night. When the screen is positive, we still do a standard sleep test.
models.clinician: Four caveats. One, the TFDA clearance is for screening suspected severe OSA, at a bRDI of 30 or more, so a positive screen still needs a standard sleep test. Two, the radar doesn't measure oxygen or CO2. Three, at home it read about 5 events per hour lower than HSAT on average. Four, the cardiac findings are associations, not validated for prediction.
models.patient: This device is like a first check. It can tell us if you might have severe sleep apnea, but it doesn't check your oxygen level, and it can't give the final answer. If it finds a problem, we'll still do a full sleep test.
models.oneliner: It's a screen that sees breathing patterns only, not oxygen, so a positive result still needs a standard test.

concepts.challenge: What are the main limitations of your radar?

concepts.title_en: Q&A: Why not just use wearables?
concepts.title_zh: 問答：為什麼不用穿戴式就好
concepts.essence: 和穿戴式比：穿戴式（腦波、心臟、動作、呼吸、血氧）每一種都要戴在身上，會不舒服、貼片可能過敏；雷達什麼都不用戴，所以可以一晚接一晚地監測。

ideas.en: Every wearable has to be worn on the body.
They are uncomfortable, and the patch can cause allergy.
With radar, there is nothing to wear.
So we can monitor night after night.

terms.note: AL-er-jee，重音在第一音節，不是 a-LER-gy
un-KUMF-ter-bul，中間的 or 幾乎不唸
不要說 every night after night

mistakes.bad: It must wear on the body.
mistakes.good: It has to be worn on the body.
mistakes.why: 裝置是「被穿戴」，要用被動 be worn。
mistakes.say: It has to be worn on the body.

mistakes.why: 泛指病人用複數。
兩種說法擇一。

models.plain: The big difference is simple: wearables have to be worn, and the radar doesn't. Watches, rings, and patches all sit on the body. They can be uncomfortable, and patches can cause allergy. With radar, there's nothing to wear, so we can monitor night after night.
models.patient: With a watch or a patch, you have to remember to put it on, and some people get a skin rash from the patch. With this device, you just go to sleep. Nothing touches you, so it's easy to use every night.
models.clinician: Type I to Type IV tests and consumer wearables all need sensors on the body. That limits comfort and long-term use. A contactless radar removes that barrier, so we can follow breathing night after night, not just for one or two nights.
models.skeptic: Wearables are great for many things. But every one of them has to be worn, and during sleep that matters: they can be uncomfortable, and people take them off. The radar needs nothing on the body, so we can monitor night after night.
models.oneliner: Wearables must be worn; the radar needs nothing on the body, so it works night after night.

concepts.challenge: Wearables are cheap and everywhere. Why bother with radar?

concepts.title_en: Q&A: privacy (and questions you can't fully answer)
concepts.title_zh: 問答：隱私（與答不出來的問題）
concepts.essence: 隱私：雷達不是攝影機、不拍影像，只把胸部動作轉成呼吸訊號。（本場講稿沒有談隱私細節和成本；遇到像成本這種手邊沒數字的問題，誠實說、給你知道的部分、提議會後再談。）

ideas.zh: 雷達不是攝影機、不拍影像
ideas.en: The radar is not a camera. It doesn't take pictures.

ideas.zh: 只取得胸部動作／呼吸訊號
ideas.en: It only picks up chest motion and turns it into a breathing signal.

ideas.zh: 不知道的部分誠實說、會後再談

models.skeptic: That's an important question. The radar is not a camera. It doesn't take pictures of the patient. What it picks up is chest motion, which we turn into a breathing signal. So what we see is a breathing wave, not a person.
models.plain: Many people hear 'radar' and think of a camera. It isn't. It only senses movement, mainly the chest rising and falling, and turns that into a breathing signal. There are no pictures of your face or your body.
models.honest: That's a fair question, but I don't have the exact cost numbers with me today. What I can say is that there's nothing to wear, and at home no technician has to be on site. I'd be happy to follow up after the session.
models.patient: Don't worry, it's not a camera. It can't see your face. It only notices your chest moving up and down while you sleep.
models.oneliner: It's not a camera: it only turns chest motion into a breathing signal.
